title: In 74 epilepsy patients, a per-electrode source score predicted the direction of stimulation responses, but this score did not follow the cortical hierarchy maps
abstract: Question: in human cortico-cortical evoked potentials (CCEPs), is the non-reciprocity of N1 responses (A evokes an N1 at B, but B does not evoke one at A) a node property, and does such a node score follow the cortical hierarchy? Data: OpenNeuro ds004080 v1.2.4 (CC0), 74 patients aged 4-51 with subdural ECoG, 303,345 directed stimulation edges (36,594 with N1); group T1w/T2w, FC gradients, thickness and MPC gradient (BrainSpace) and HCP group structural connectome (ENIGMA), Schaefer-400. Method: for each electrode pair that was stimulated and recorded both ways, y = N1 rate e->j minus j->e (39,183 responsive comparisons). In each patient, a HodgeRank fit y = phi_e - phi_j + distance and current terms gives a net-source score phi. Test 1: purged 5-fold held-out prediction of the sign of y. Test 2 (pre-set; primary maps T1w/T2w and FC gradient 1): within-patient Spearman rho of phi with parcel maps, 1000 vertex and parcel spins, and a group parcel map. Test 3: latency asymmetry. Results: the node score predicted the held-out direction at 0.691 against 0.533 for distance and current only (71 of 74 patients; 0.692 at 20 mm or more). Phi did not follow T1w/T2w (mean rho 0.003, CI -0.052 to 0.057, spin p 0.97) or FC gradient 1 (0.025, CI -0.020 to 0.071, p 0.62); the group parcel map was also null and the result held after seizure-onset-zone, resection and grid controls. SC strength had a weak, non-robust positive link (rho 0.063, spin p 0.024-0.14), opposite in sign to the diffusion-model prediction that hubs are receivers. Phi tracked the stimulation side (rho 0.60 with own out-rate, -0.39 with in-rate), was smooth over 15-30 mm, but the same parcel was not consistently a source across patients (split-half rho 0.10). Latency asymmetry did not follow phi or the hierarchy maps. Conclusion: CCEP direction is largely an electrode-level source/sink order, but this order is local and is not the sensory-to-transmodal hierarchy. Limitations: clinical coverage with few visual and medial electrodes, group maps, bipolar stimulation, automatic N1 detection, one centre.

display.caption: a: held-out sign accuracy of the N1 asymmetry in each of 74 patients, with distance and current terms only (gray) and with the electrode net-source scores added (blue); purged 5-fold cross-validation. b: N1 rates in the two directions against the held-out predicted asymmetry (deciles, 39,183 responsive comparisons). c: pooled accuracy in the main run, at native distance of 20 mm or more, and with comparisons without any N1.

a: mean within-patient Spearman rho between the electrode net-source score phi and parcel maps, with patient bootstrap 95% CI, for the main run, with seizure-onset-zone, resection and grid effects removed, and at 20 mm or more. b: Spearman rho between the group parcel map of phi (258 parcels) and each map. The primary maps (T1w/T2w, FC gradient 1) give values near zero; spin p > 0.4.

a (exploratory): median within-patient rho of phi with the raw N1 rate an electrode evokes (out-rate) and receives (in-rate), with the mean phi of electrodes 15-30 mm away, and the split-half reliability of the group parcel map across patients (95% range). b: mean within-patient rho of the N1 latency asymmetry with the phi difference (patient bootstrap CI) and with map differences (parcel-spin p).
